preDeclaredThreshold: a test is positive only if the observed score exceeds the 95th percentile of dose-shuffled nulls with p < 0.05, dose shuffled within timepoint
centring: each timepoint is centred by its own mean before fitting, so no between-timepoint variation reaches the model

P1_withinTimepointRanking.protocol: per-timepoint Spearman between predicted and true dose, model trained on the other three timepoints, 4 folds

P2_middleLevelInterpolation.protocol: ridge through the 0 and 100 Gy anchors, then the fraction of 10 Gy samples predicted strictly between the two anchors

comparisonToPhase10.statement: Phase 10 measured a global ordinal trend of 0.1965 and left the per-timepoint spread unexplained. P1 replaces that global number with a within-timepoint ranking that cannot be produced by time, and P2 asks about a dose level the model never saw.

rejectedExperiments.experiment: AUC between an unseen dose level and its nearest training level, three configurations
rejectedExperiments.result: AUC 0.0903, 0.0000 and 1.0000 with a permutation null centred at 0.3403 rather than 0.5
rejectedExperiments.whyRejected: Every configuration reused a training level as the reference class, so the AUC was fixed by construction: a model trained to put 10 Gy below 100 Gy scores 0.0 when 10 Gy is the reference, and one trained through 0 Gy scores 1.0 for the same reason. The null being off 0.5 is the tell that the statistic is not a permutation test at all.

rejectedExperiments.experiment: leave-one-dose-level-out ridge regression, scored by Spearman
rejectedExperiments.result: observed -0.5371 with a permutation null centred at -0.7434, so the null was degenerate and the p-value meaningless
rejectedExperiments.whyRejected: Extrapolating a linear fit from two dose anchors puts a held-out level thousands of Gy away, and under label shuffling the anchors move but the feature geometry does not, so the null piles up at a strongly negative correlation. A test whose null is not centred on zero cannot support a claim in either direction.
rejectedExperiments.replacement: P2, the AUC-only formulation, whose null is centred on 0.5

rejectedExperiments.whyRejected: A classifier trained on two dose levels can only emit those two labels, so it can never be credited with the third. The score measures the protocol, not the data. Reported here instead of deleted because 0.000 looks like a dramatic finding and is only a category error.

rejectedExperiments.experiment: classification edge for a held-out dose using a two-class boundary
rejectedExperiments.whyRejected: Any monotone binary boundary places a held-out 100 Gy sample on the high side by construction once 0 Gy and 10 Gy are the training classes, so it would reward the trivial ordering.

status: radiation-dose-osd782-v1 stays excluded from the registry; nothing here reaches predictive quality, and the exclusion reason is now specific: the evidence for dose is a weak ordinal tendency that does not survive an unseen dose level
